resultText:
I found six bugs on the new Stats page, and I saw every one happen in the running app. Two are high severity. The findings file is written to `out/findings.json` and is valid JSON.

| # | Severity | Bug |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | High | **A slow answer replaces newer results.** I changed From to 2026-06-01 (slowed to 3 s), then quickly to 2026-09-01. The 1 Sep results appeared first, then the late 1 Jun answer overwrote them, while the From field and URL still said 2026-09-01. |
| 2 | High | **Requests never time out.** I made the stats request hang. After 15 s the page still said "Loading stats…" and still showed the previous range's table and best plants, as if they were current. |
| 3 | Medium | **The error message has no retry button.** On a 500 the page only says "Could not load harvest stats." Changing a date does recover (failed results aren't cached), but there is no Try again. |
| 4 | Medium | **An unreadable response crashes the page.** A 200 response with an HTML body throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')` and leaves "Loading stats…" stuck. A response with null fields shows an empty table with "– total" instead of an error. |
| 5 | Low | **Months with no harvests are left out of the table.** The 2026 range only shows Jun–Sept columns. A wide range jumps straight from Aug 2025 to Jun 2026. |
| 6 | Low | **A blank From date is handled confusingly.** Clearing it silently means 1 Jan this year. With To set in 2025, the page then says "The From date must be on or before the To date." while From is empty. |

These all worked:
- **Bad dates:** the API answers impossible, malformed, empty, reversed and 6-digit-year dates with a 422, never a 5xx.
- **Narrow screens:** neither the Stats page nor the dashboard scrolls sideways at 375 px, even with a long emoji/markup/Arabic plant name. The long name in the best-plant cards is cut off with "…".
- **Expired session:** a 401 on the stats request sends the user to sign in.
- **Dashboard and nav:** the dashboard's best plant and its link to Stats, and the "Stats" nav link, work.

I couldn't check whether the error looks the same when the page is opened directly, because that first load's API call runs on the app's server, where the browser can't intercept it. I checked the in-app link path only.

For the long-name test I added a plant ("Supercalifragilisticexpialidocious-heirloom-mega-tomato 🍅 …", id 4) and a 5 kg harvest on 2026-10-01 to the sample data. They're still there, so that plant now tops this year's stats and the dashboard.
